en: Sitātapatrā (Sita 147): Om, homage to all the glorious Buddhas and Bodhisattvas!

Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Trāyastriṃśa gods in the Sudharmā assembly hall of the gods, together with a great saṅgha of bhikṣus, a great saṅgha of bodhisattvas, hundreds of bhikṣus, and Śakra, the lord of the devas.
There, the Blessed One, having sat down on the seat prepared for him, entered the samādhi called the Uṣṇīṣāvalokita.
Immediately upon the Blessed One’s entering [meditative absorption], these mantra syllables issued forth from the center of his *uṣṇīṣa*:
"Homage to the Blessed One, the *Uṣṇīṣa*, the pure, the stainless, the immaculate, svāhā!
Homage to the Blessed One, the *Uṣṇīṣa* who is without aspiration!"
Homage to the Buddha.
Homage to the Dharma. Homage to the Saṅgha.
Homage to the seven koṭis of perfectly awakened Buddhas; homage to all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, headed by Maitreya, together with their assemblies of Śrāvakas;
homage to the Arhats in the world; homage to those who have entered the stream.
Homage to those who have attained the state of once-returning! Homage to those who have attained the state of non-returning!
Homage to those who have gone rightly in the world!
Homage to those who have practiced correctly!
Homage to the divine sages!
Homage to the divine Brahmā!
Homage to the Buddha!
Homage to the Blessed One Rudra, together with Umāpati!
Homage to Varuṇa!
Homage to the Blessed One, Nārāyaṇa; homage to the one who is saluted by the Great Five Mudrās;
homage to the Blessed One, Nandikeśvara Mahākāla.
Homage to the one who causes the destruction of the city of Tripura;
to the one who dwells in the great cremation ground of Adhimuktika in Kaśmīra;
homage to the one accompanied by the host of Mothers.
Homage to the Blessed One of the Tathāgata family! Homage to the Blessed One of the Padma family! Homage to the Blessed One of the Vajra family!
Homage to the Blessed One of the Jewel Family! Homage to the Blessed One of the Elephant Family! Homage to the Blessed One of the Action Family!
Homage to the Blessed One of the Jewel Family! Homage to the Blessed One of the Youth Family! Homage to the Blessed One of the Naga Family!
Homage to the Blessed One of the Passion Family!
Homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, King of the Weapons of the Firm Heroic Army!
Homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Amitābha!
Homage to the Blessed One, Akṣobhya, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Homage to the Blessed One, Vajradharasāgaragarjita, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Homage to the Blessed One, Bhaiṣajyaguruvaiḍūryaprabharāja, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Homage to the Blessed One, Amoghasiddhi, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One.
Homage to the Blessed One, Supuṣpitasālendrarāja, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One.
Homage to the Blessed One, Padmottararāja, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One.
Homage to the Blessed One, Vipaśyin, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One.
Homage to the Blessed One, Śikhin, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One.
Homage to the Blessed One, Viśvabhū, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One.
Homage to the Blessed One, Krakucchanda, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Homage to the Blessed One, Kanakamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. Homage to the Blessed One, Kāśyapa, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Homage to the Blessed One, Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Homage to the Blessed One, Ratnacandra, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Homage to the Blessed One, Ratnaketurāja, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Homage to the Blessed One, Samantabhadra, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened Buddha.
Homage to the Blessed One, Vairocana, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened Buddha.
Homage to the Blessed One, Vikasitakamalottaragandhaketurāja, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened Buddha.
Having paid homage to these, I shall proclaim this Bhagavatī, the Aparājitā Pratyaṅgirā named Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣasitātapatrā,
who pacifies all strife, quarrels, conflicts, and disputes,
and wards off all malevolent spirits and planetary influences.
It cuts through all the spells of others;
it protects against untimely death;
it liberates all sentient beings from bondage.
It is the destroyer of all evil dreams;
the one that brings about the destruction of yakṣas, rākṣasas, and seizing spirits;
the one that brings about the destruction of the eighty-four thousand seizing spirits.
She who brings peace to the twenty-eight lunar mansions;
she who wards off all enemies and destroys the eight great planets;
and she who annihilates terrible, evil, and bad dreams.
It is that which carries one across poison, weapons, fire, and water;
it is that which carries one across the fear of all miserable rebirths;
and it is that which provides protection against all eight types of untimely death.

Aparājitā, Mahāghorā, Mahābalā, Mahātejā, Mahācaṇḍā, Mahāśvetā, Mahādīptā, Mahāmālā, Mahājvālā, and Mahāpāṇḍaravāsinī; Āryatārā, Bhṛkuṭī, Jayā, and likewise Vijayā; and she who is renowned as Vajramālā, the destroyer of all Māras.
Padmā, Bhāvajacinhā, Mālā, Aparājitā,
Vajratuṇḍī, Viśālī, Śāntā, and Vaidehapūjitā.
Saumyarūpā, Mahāśvetā, Jvālā, Pāṇḍaravāsinī,
Āryatārā, Mahābalā, and the other, Vajraśṛṅkhalā.
Likewise, Vajrakaumārī, Kulandarī, Vajrahastā, Vajravidyā, Kāñcanamālikā, Kusumbharatnā, and Radanā. (Sitā 149)
And also Vairocanakulaprabhā,
as well as the renowned Tathāgatakuloṣṇīṣā and Vijṛmbhamāṇikā.
Vajrā, Kanakaprabhā, Locanā, Vajratuṇḍikā,
as well as Śvetā, Kamalākṣiṇī, and Buddhalocanā.
Likewise Vajraprabhā, Candrā, and also Vajradharā;
Vajramālā, Mahāmāyā, and the goddess Kanakaprabhā.
Likewise Sulocanā, Śvetā, and Kamalekṣaṇā;
Vinītā, Śāntacittā, Ātmaguṇajñā, and Śaśiprabhā.
Thus, may these hosts of Mahāmudrās and all the hosts of Mothers provide protection for me and for all sentient beings.
Oṃ! Praised by the hosts of ṛṣis, O White Parasol of the Uṣṇīṣa of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ hūṃ hrīṃ ṣṭroṃ jambhani!
hūṃ hūṃ hrīṃ ṣṭroṃ stambhani!

Oṃ hūṃ hūṃ hrīṃ ṣṭro, the paralyzer of rival spells! Hūṃ hūṃ hrīṃ ṣṭroṃ, the destroyer of all yakṣas, rākṣasas, and seizing spirits! Hūṃ hūṃ hrīṃ ṣṭroṃ, the destroyer of the eighty-four thousand seizing spirits!
HŪṂ HŪṂ HRĪṂ ṢṬRO! She who brings peace to the twenty-eight lunar mansions.
HŪṂ HŪṂ HRĪṂ ṢṬRO! She who destroys the eight great planets.
HŪṂ HŪṂ HRĪṂ ṢṬROṂ! Protect me and all sentient beings!

Homage to the Blessed One, the White Parasol of the Uṣṇīṣa of all Tathāgatas, the Great Praty-aṅgirā, with a thousand great arms, a thousand great heads, and hundreds of thousands of millions of eyes; indivisible, blazing with the sound of *ṭaṃkāra*, the Great Vajra, the Noble One within the mandala of the three worlds!
Oṃ! May there be well-being for me and for all sentient beings!
From fear of kings, from fear of thieves,
and from fear of fire.
From the fear of water, from the fear of poison and weapons,
and from the fear of enemies.
From fear of the enemy's army, from fear of famine,
and from fear of adversaries.
from the fear of thunderbolts, from the fear of untimely death,
and from the fear of earthquakes;
Out of fear of falling meteors, fear of royal punishment, and fear of fierce wild beasts.
from fear of nāgas, from fear of lightning,
and from fear of burning sand;
From the fear of Garuḍa,
from the fear of all calamities, afflictions, misfortunes, and distresses of death,
and from the fear of planetary influences;
From fear of gods, from fear of nāgas,
and from fear of yakṣas.
From the fear of rākṣasas, from the fear of gandharvas,
and from the seizure of asuras.
from the seizure of a mahoraga, from the seizure of a human, and from the seizure of a non-human;
From the seizure by spirits, from the seizure by hungry ghosts,
and from the seizure by piśācas.
From the Kumbhāṇḍa spirit, from the Pūtana spirit,
and from the Kaṭapūtana spirit.
From the seizure of the aggregates,
from the seizure of madness,
and from the seizure of the shadow.
From the seizure of epilepsy, from the seizure of ostāḍaka,
and from the seizure of ḍākinī.
From the seizure of Kaṭaḍākinī, from the seizure of Revatī, and from the seizure of Śakuni.
From the *mātṛnandi* seizure,
from the *lambikā* seizure, and from the *śamikā* seizure; (Sītā 150)
Because of grasping at an object, because of grasping at Kaṭavāsinī,
and because of grasping at Kaṇṭakamālinī.
From all seizing spirits:
from Vratāhāriṇī and Garbhāhāriṇī.
Of her who feeds on blood, her who feeds on flesh, and her who feeds on fat.
of one who takes away the marrow, of one who takes away the birth, and of one who takes away life;
of one who carries garlands, of one who carries flower-garlands, and of one who carries perfumes;
Of one who gathers flowers, of one who gathers incense,
and of one who gathers fruits.
Of her who carries away the grain, of her who carries away the oblation,
of her who carries away the worship.
of one who eats excrement,
of one who drinks urine, and of one who eats phlegm;
of one who feeds on snot, of one who feeds on wind,
and of one who feeds on excrement;
of one who takes away impurity,
of one who takes away the flow [of life], and of one who takes away wealth;
Of those who steal the mind—
of all these, I cut through all obstacles with a sword and nail them down with a vajra.
The spell created by wandering mendicants, I cut it with a sword and nail it down with a vajra.

I cut asunder with the sword and nail down with the vajra the spell created by the ḍākas and ḍākinīs; I cut asunder with the sword and nail down with the vajra the spell created by Brahmā; I cut asunder with the sword and nail down with the vajra the spell created by Śakra.

I cut asunder with a sword and nail down with a vajra the spell created by Nārāyaṇa; I cut asunder with a sword and nail down with a vajra the spell created by Mahāpaśupati; I cut asunder with a sword and nail down with a vajra the spell created by Mahākāla.

I cut with the sword and nail with the vajra the spells made by the Mātṛkā-gaṇas; I cut with the sword and nail with the vajra the spells made by the Kāpālikas; I cut with the sword and nail with the vajra the spells made by the Śabaras.
I cut with a sword and nail with a vajra the spell made by the Pukkasas; I cut with a sword and nail with a vajra the spell made by the Atharvans;
I cut with a sword and nail with a vajra the spell made by Vajrakaumārī.

I cut with the sword and nail down with the vajra the spell created by Yama’s henchmen; I cut with the sword and nail down with the vajra the spell created by Yama’s messengers; I cut with the sword and nail down with the vajra the spell created by cruel nāgas.

I cut with a sword and nail with a vajra the spells performed by Adhikarmakṛts; I cut with a sword and nail with a vajra the spells performed by Vināyakas; I cut with a sword and nail with a vajra the spells performed by Kumāras.
I cut with the sword and nail down with the vajra the spell created by the Four Great Kings.
I cut with the sword and nail down with the vajra the spell created by the Four Sisters. I cut with the sword and nail down with the vajra the spell created by Garuḍa.

I cut with a sword and nail down with a vajra the spell performed by Jayakara, Madhukara, Siddhikara, and Sarvārthasādhana. I cut with a sword and nail down with a vajra the spell performed by Śṛṅgiriṭi, Nandikeśvara, Kārttikeya, Candra, Sūrya, and Gaṇapati. I cut with a sword and nail down with a vajra the spell performed by Nagnaśravaṇa (Nagnaśramaṇa).
I cut with a sword and nail with a vajra the spell created by an Arhat.
I cut with a sword and nail with a vajra the spell created by Avalokiteśvara. I cut with a sword the spell created by one free from passion. (Sitā 151)
I nail it down with the vajra!
I cut with the sword the spell made by Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Guhyakas; I nail it down with the vajra! Wherever [it may be], I cut with the sword the spell made there; I nail it down with the vajra!
With this sword I cut asunder, and with this vajra I pin down, the spell performed by him who caused it to be made;
with this sword I cut asunder, and with this vajra I pin down, the spell performed by Muṇḍa and Śravaṇa;
the spell performed by the male messengers, female messengers, servants, and handmaidens.
I cut with the sword and I nail down with the vajra the spell created by the best of all ṛṣis; I cut with the sword and I nail down with the vajra the spell created by the hosts of all deities.
With this sword I cut asunder the spell cast by those who wish me harm; with the vajra I pin it down.

Oṃ, Blessed One, protect, protect me and all sentient beings from all fears, from all calamities, misfortunes, and afflictions, and from all the wicked, the malicious, and all enemies who wish us ill! Homage to you, the Tathāgata’s Uṣṇīṣa, the White Parasol!
Homage to all the Buddhas!
O you who possess the radiant, fully blossomed white parasol, shining like the dark fire and the sun!
Oṃ jvala 2 dhaka 2 khāda 2 dara 2 vidara 2 chinda 2 bhinda 2 hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ 2 svāhā!
HŪṂ HŪṂ, all malevolent ones! PHAṬ to those who transgress!
PHAṬ to all those who have poorly inscribed [the mantra]! PHAṬ to all those with poor reflections!
Phaṭ to all directions!
Phaṭ to all intermediate directions! Phaṭ to all evil beings!
Phaṭ to all vomitings of evil! Phaṭ to all blameworthy acts! Phaṭ to all misdeeds!
Phaṭ to all those who are difficult to look upon! Phaṭ to all blazing ones [and all fevers]!
Phaṭ to all epilepsy-demons!
Phaṭ to all those who cause epilepsy!
Phaṭ to all ḍākinīs! Phaṭ to all revatīs!
Phaṭ to all those dwelling in the thicket! Phaṭ to all the Jāmakas! {Phaṭ to all the Yāmakas!} Phaṭ to all the birds!
Phaṭ to all Mātṛnandikas! Phaṭ to all poisons! Phaṭ to all venoms!
Phaṭ from all yogas! Phaṭ from all attachments! Phaṭ from all fears!
Phaṭ from all calamities! Phaṭ from all misfortunes and afflictions! Phaṭ from all terrors!
Phaṭ from all diseases! Phaṭ from all ascetics! Phaṭ from all seizing spirits!
Phaṭ to all heretics! Phaṭ to all adversaries! Phaṭ to all transgressions!
Phaṭ to all those who cause madness! Phaṭ to all the Vidyādharas! Phaṭ to Jayakara, Madhukara, and Sarvārthasādhaka!
Phaṭ to all those who practice the sciences!
Phaṭ to all the kings of the sciences! Phaṭ to all the practitioners and masters of the sciences!
Phaṭ to the four sisters!
Phaṭ to Vajrakaumārī, the queen of vidyās! Phaṭ to all obstacles and obstructors!
For the purpose of terrifying the enemies, *phaṭ*!
*Phaṭ* to all the asuras! *Phaṭ* to all the garuḍas!
Phaṭ to all great serpents! Phaṭ to all humans and non-humans!
Phaṭ to all Maruts!
Phaṭ to all kumbhāṇḍas!
Phaṭ to Vajraśṛṅkhalā, the Great Pratyāṅgirā! Phaṭ to all calamities!
Phaṭ to the great Pratyāṅgirasas! Phaṭ, cut, cut! Phaṭ, split, split!
HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ / HE HE PHAṬ / HO HO PHAṬ /
To the Unfailing One, phaṭ! To the Unobstructed One, phaṭ!
To the Bestower of Boons, phaṭ!
To the one who causes the asuras to flee, *phaṭ*!
To all the gods, *phaṭ*!
To all the nāgas, *phaṭ*!
Phaṭ to all yakṣas! Phaṭ to all rākṣasas! Phaṭ to all gandharvas!
Phaṭ to all kinnaras! Phaṭ to all bhūtas! Phaṭ to all pretas!
Phaṭ to all piśācas! Phaṭ to all pūtanās!
Phaṭ to all kaṭapūtanas!
Phaṭ to all the aggregates!
Phaṭ to the vajra-chains! Phaṭ to the Great King Pratyāṅgirā!
Phaṭ to Kāla! Phaṭ to Mahākāla! Phaṭ to the hosts of Mothers!
Homage to her who is saluted by the great host of Mothers, Phaṭ!
To Vaiṣṇavī, Phaṭ!
To Māheśvarī, Phaṭ!
Phaṭ to Brahmāyaṇī!
Phaṭ to Agni! Phaṭ to Mahākālī!
Phaṭ to Kāladaṇḍī! Phaṭ to Aindrī! Phaṭ to Raudrī!
Cāmuṇḍīye phaṭ!
Vārāhīye phaṭ!
Mahāvārāhīye phaṭ!
Phaṭ to Kālarātrī! Phaṭ to Rātrī! Phaṭ to Yamadāḍhī!
To Kāpālīyā, phaṭ! To Mahākāpālīyā, phaṭ!
To Kaumārīyā, phaṭ!
Phaṭ to the southern direction! Phaṭ to the western direction! Phaṭ to the southwestern direction!
To Vāruṇī, phaṭ!
To Mārūtī, phaṭ!
To Mahāmārūtī, phaṭ!
Phaṭ to Saumyā! Phaṭ to Aiśānī!
Phaṭ to Pukkasī!
To Artharvaṇī, Phaṭ!
To Śabarī, Phaṭ!
To Kṛṣṇaśabarī, Phaṭ!
Phaṭ to the messengers of Yama! Phaṭ to those who roam at night! Phaṭ to those who roam during the three junctions of the day!
Phaṭ to Dharaṇī! Phaṭ to Adhimuktikā, who dwells in the great cemetery of Kāśmīra!
Phaṭ from all these fears!
*phaṭ* from all faults!
*Oṃ ṣṭrau*, bind, bind; protect, protect me and all sentient beings from the wicked, *svāhā*!

Whatever beings there may be who are wicked toward me and all sentient beings—those with wicked minds, those who are fierce and have fierce minds, those who are sinful and have sinful minds, those who are angry and have angry minds, those who are enemies and have inimical minds—[may they be bound].
May these protect me and all sentient beings; may they live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns. Whatever yakṣa-grahas there are, those who subsist on vows, [may they protect us].
those who feed on embryos, those who feed on blood, those who feed on bamboo [or marrow], and those who feed on fat;
those who eat flesh, those who eat fat,
and those who eat marrow;
Those who feed on birth, those who feed on life, and those who feed on strength.
Those who feed on garlands,
those who feed on perfumes, and those who feed on flowers.
Those who subsist on incense,
those who subsist on fruits, and those who subsist on sacrificial offerings.
Those who subsist on wealth,
those who subsist on thought,
and those who subsist on worship.
those who feed on excrement, those who feed on phlegm, and those who feed on saliva;
those who feed on snot,
those who feed on wind, and those who feed on excrement;
They consume impure food, they consume putrid food;
they possess evil minds.
Those with malicious minds, those with fierce minds, and the planetary spirits of the gods.
Nāga-grahas, yakṣa-grahas, and rākṣasa-grahas.
the grahas of the gandharvas,
the grahas of the asuras, and the grahas of the garuḍas;
the Kinnara-grahas,
the Mahoraga-grahas,
and the human-grahas.
seizures by non-human spirits, seizures by Maruts, and seizures by Piśācas;
the spirits that seize beings, the *kumbhāṇḍa* spirits that seize beings, and the *pūtana* spirits that seize beings;
the Kaṭapūtana spirits,
the Skanda spirits,
and the Unmāda spirits;
seizing spirits of shadows, seizing spirits of epilepsy, and seizing spirits of convulsions;
the ḍākinī-grahas, the revatī-grahas, and the śamikā-grahas;
the Jāmakagrahas,
the Śakunigrahas, and the Mātṛnandigrahas;
The grahas of Kambukāminī, the grahas of Alambanā, and the grahas of Kaṭaḍākinī.
The Kaṇṭakamālinī grahas, all grahas; fevers that recur every day, Ekāhika.
Those occurring every second day, those occurring every third day, and those occurring every fourth day.
Those lasting seven days,
those lasting half a month, and those lasting a month.
Those with fevers recurring every two months, those occurring at specific moments, and those that are constant.
irregular fevers,
(Sitā 153) fevers caused by pretas, and fevers caused by piśācas;
Human fevers,
non-human fevers, and those caused by wind (vātika).
Those caused by bile, those caused by phlegm, and those caused by the combination of all three humors.

May all fevers be removed from my head, and may [they remove] half-headaches, loss of appetite, eye disease, nose disease, mouth disease, throat disease, heart disease, throat constriction, earache, toothache, chest pain, heart pain, pain in the vital organs, back pain, abdominal pain, bladder pain, and rectal pain for me and for all sentient beings.
May they remove my pain in the womb, pain in the vagina, pain in the thighs, pain in the calves, pain in the hands, pain in the feet, and pain in the major and minor limbs.

May they dispel *bhūtas*, *pretas*, *vetālas*, *ḍākinīs*, fevers, burning sensations, itching, scabies, leprosy, bile disorders, spleen ailments, fistula-in-ano, spider-bites, ringworm, erysipelas, iron-like sores, all forms of asthma, terror, coughing, fainting, poisons, sorcery, fire, water, pestilence, quarrels, enmity, wilderness dangers, untimely death, the *tryambuka* and *trailāṭaka* insects, scorpions, snakes, mongooses, lions, tigers, bears, hyenas, crocodiles, wolves, thieves, and those who cause harm to living beings.

{Śambuka(tailāṭaŚ)} / By the power of the Sitātapatrā, Mahoṣṇīṣā, and Mahāpratyaṅgirā vidyās, for all others whatsoever, I effect a binding of the vidyās within a range of twelve yojanas or fifty yojanas; I effect a binding of their splendor; [I effect] a binding of all vidyās.
I perform the binding by means of the supreme vidyā; I perform the binding of the boundary; I perform the binding of the earth; I perform the binding of the ten directions;
I perform the paralyzing of enemy armies. It is as follows: Oṃ anane 2 khakhane 2 vīṣama 2 vīre 2 maunya 2 śānte 2 dānte 2 Vajradhara, O binder of all binders, Vajrapāṇi, phaṭ!
Oṃ hūṃ ṣṭroṃ phaṭ 2 svāhā!
Oṃ vajrapāśe bandha 2 vajrapāśaṃ ca sarvaduṣṭavighnavināyakān hūṃ phaṭ 2 rakṣa 2 māṃ sarvasattvāṃśca svāhā!
Whoever writes down this Great Queen of Spells, Aparājitāpratyaṅgirā, named Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣasitātapatrā—
Whether written on birch bark, cloth, or bark, and whether worn on the body or around the neck, one who maintains and recites it shall not tolerate impurity;
no ritual magic or sorcery shall prevail against them.
He will enter the city;
he will enter into yoga;
he will not meet his end through untimely death.
He will be dear to all the planetary spirits (*graha*) and to all obstacles and impediments (*vighnavināyaka*).

For eighty-four thousand million eons (*kalpakoṭīsahasra*), he will be pleasing and, in birth after birth, he will remember his former lives (*jātismara*). Eighty-four hundred thousand million trillion *vidyā*-deities of the Vajra family will constantly, perpetually, and continuously provide him with protection, defense, and guardianship.
The eighty-four thousand vajra-messengers and servants will constantly protect them, and he will be dear to them as well;
he will be pleasing to them and shall never experience the state of a yakṣa, a rākṣasa, a bhūta, a piśāca, a pūtana, or a kaṭapūtana, nor the poverty of a human being.
He will be endowed with a mass of merit equal to that of immeasurable Buddhas, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā.

And one who maintains this Great Queen of Spells, the Aparājitā Pratyaṅgirā named Sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣasitātapatrā, though not practicing celibacy, will become one who practices celibacy; though not observing silence, will become one who observes silence;
and though impure, will become pure.
One who has not observed the fast will become one who has observed it;
even one who has committed the five sins of immediate retribution will have their evil shaken off.
The obstructions of past karma go to complete exhaustion without remainder.
Any woman who maintains this Great Vidyārājñī Aparājitā Mahāpratyāṅgirā, known as the Tathāgata-uṣṇīṣa-sitātapatra, shall obtain a son if she desires a son;
she obtains longevity, merit, and strength.
Having passed away from here, one will be reborn in the world-system Sukhāvatī;
and that person will be free from passion, hatred, delusion, pride, and arrogance—
whosoever [is thus protected] during human slaughter, animal slaughter, or cow slaughter, and during all calamities, misfortunes, distresses, and the arrival of enemy armies.

Having placed that Aparājitā [dhāraṇī] of the Blessed One, the Jina, the Perfectly Awakened One— named the White Parasol of the Uṣṇīṣa of All Tathāgatas— upon the tip of a banner, and having performed a great worship with extensive offerings and honors, one should cause it to enter through all the city gates,
whether in a monastery, a village, a city, a district, a town, a cemetery, or a mountain.

Whether in a village or in a forest hermitage, one should cause this Aparājitā Pratyaṅgirā, the Queen of Vidyās, to enter with great honor. As soon as she has entered, all calamities, misfortunes, and distresses will be pacified; even hostile armies will be quelled.
The nāga king Ananta, the nāga king Śaṅkhapāla, the nāga king Mahākṛṣṇa, the two nāga kings Nanda and Upananda, and all those other nāga kings will, from time to time, send down rain;
from time to time, they will exert themselves;
from time to time, they will thunder, and they will pacify all diseases and calamities.
Oṃ ṣṭroṃ, bind! bind! protect me and all sentient beings from all malevolent ones, svāhā!
Oṃ hūṃ ṣṭroṃ, bind! bind! protect me and all sentient beings from the wicked ones, O Vajrapāṇi, hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Oṃ, you who are the mass of splendor from the crown of the head of the Tathāgata-uṣṇīṣa Avalokita!
Oṃ jvala 2 dhak 2 khāda 2 dara 2 vidara 2 chinda 2 bhinda 2 hūṃ 2 phaṭ 3 rakṣa 2 māṃ sarvasattvāṃśca svāhā!
Oṃ sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣasitātapatre hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ rakṣa 2 māṃ sarvasattvāṃśca hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!

It is as follows: *Oṃ anale anale, acare acare, khasame khasame, vīre vīre, saumye saumye, adhiṣṭhite by the empowerment of all Buddhas, O White Parasol of the Uṣṇīṣa of all Tathāgatas, [subdue] all those with malicious minds! Hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!* By means of the Buddha-yoga, this should be recited three times during all calamities.
And all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, as well as the world with its gods, humans, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas, rejoiced in what was spoken by the Blessed One.
Thus ends the Noble Great Queen of Spells, the Unconquered *Pratyaṅgirā*, named the White Parasol of the Uṣṇīṣa of All Tathāgatas.
